name: Rollback Strategy Conventions
description: This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing rollback strategy code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing rollback strategy style guide.
content:
This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing rollback strategy code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing rollback strategy style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate rollback strategy outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. Prefer explicit, readable rollback strategy solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. Before starting rollback strategy work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Prefer the simplest rollback strategy approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen rollback strategy approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Measure before optimizing any rollback strategy bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. Check that rollback strategy terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. Document any non-obvious rollback strategy decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
9. When rollback strategy decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
10. Re-check edge cases relevant to rollback strategy (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
11. Keep rollback strategy outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
12. Keep rollback strategy changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic rollback strategy advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of rollback strategy correctness.
- Avoid introducing new rollback strategy abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these rollback strategy guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
